newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shrs end up on technical rebound, low volume.
newsitem.headline: Lima shrs end up on technical rebound, low volume.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed higher on low volume on Wednesday in a technical rebound that saw some local players buying cheap stocks after days of dipping prices, brokers said.
But they added the overall trend for the next few weeks was negative because of the economy's slow growth.
Wednesday, the General Index rose 0.12 percent to 1,447.1 points and the blue-chip Selective Index rose 1.08 percent to 2,040.2 points, according to preliminary stock figures.

Wednesday's trade was "more of a technical rebound than anything -- a consequence of various days of falls," said Letts Adams of local brokerage Peruval. "Local investors, particularly, positioned themselves."
The recent slump on the market has been due to the economy's slow growth.
Earlier on Wednesday, Economy Minister Jorge Camet told Congress the government estimated the economy would grow around 2.5 percent this year, down from 7.0 percent last year.
This would be well down on the government's original six- percent growth estimate for the year and also below the bottom-end goal of three percent agreed with the IMF mid-way through 1996.
The government announced earlier this month that the economy grew 1.9 percent in the first nine months of the year, compared with 8.9 percent in the same period of 1995.
Wednesday, benchmark Telefonica del Peru closed up 0.57 percent at 5.27 soles, in low volume of 219,000 shares, according to preliminary figures.
Electricity distributor Luz del Sur, which saw the sale of the state's 30 percent stake in the company start Monday, rose 0.30 percent to 3.36 soles on volume of 155,000 shares.
In a total of 1,398 trades, volume was estimated at 29.0 million soles ($11.2 million)
